title: Lydia Puppet Stage
subject: Contracts
stem:
At a private Christian craft fair, Lydia asked Barnabas, a longtime family friend, “Would you lend me $1,600 to buy a portable puppet stage for my paid parable-story classes? I’ll repay you with interest one year from today.” Paul, Lydia’s uncle, said, “If Lydia does not repay you as promised, I will.” Barnabas immediately handed Lydia $1,600 in cash. Lydia bought the puppet stage. When the debt came due, Lydia and Paul both refused to pay anything.

In Barnabas’s action against Paul to recover $1,600 plus interest, which statement best summarizes Paul’s best defense?
call: In Barnabas’s action against Paul to recover $1,600 plus interest, which statement best summarizes Paul’s best defense?

choices.A: The loan to Lydia was made without any agreement concerning the applicable interest rate.
choices.B: Paul’s conditional promise to Barnabas was not made for the primary purpose of benefiting Paul.
choices.C: Paul received no consideration for his conditional promise to Barnabas.
choices.D: Paul’s conditional promise to Barnabas was not to be performed in less than one year from the time it was made.

rightExplanation:
B is correct. Gold Key: An oral promise to pay another person’s debt is usually in the Statute of Frauds. The main-purpose exception removes the promise from the writing requirement only when the guarantor’s leading purpose is the guarantor’s own economic advantage.

Paul’s words create a secondary promise: if Lydia does not repay Barnabas, Paul will. The facts show the money went to Lydia for her puppet stage. Nothing in the stem gives Paul a personal economic stake. Silver Key: sort the defenses by whose promise they attack. The lawsuit is against Paul, so the best defense is the one attacking Paul’s oral guaranty, not Lydia’s loan terms.

c3.label: CUT
c3.text: A is not responsive. It attacks the loan’s interest term, not Paul’s best defense. C is not responsive. It attacks personal receipt of consideration, but the consideration issue is not whether Paul got the cash. D is not responsive. It reaches for the one-year lane, while the call’s stronger lane is Paul’s suretyship promise.

c3.label: CLASH
c3.text: The real axis is: defense to Paul’s guaranty versus defects in Lydia’s loan. The facts select Paul’s guaranty.

c3.label: CALL
c3.text: Use the Gold Key. “If Lydia does not repay, I will” is a suretyship trigger. No signed writing. No self-benefit facts for Paul. B remains.

studentScript: Call asks Paul’s best defense. Paul said, if Lydia does not pay, I will. That is the guaranty lane. Gold Key: oral guaranty needs writing unless Paul’s main purpose was Paul’s own economic gain. The facts show Lydia got the money and puppet stage, so pick B.

A.signal: The call is against Paul; this attacks Lydia’s loan term.
A.lawyer: A reasonable interest term can be supplied when the bargain is otherwise sufficiently defined; this does not defeat Paul’s guaranty issue.

B.signal: This is the only choice that attacks Paul’s oral guaranty through the main-purpose gate.
B.lawyer: Paul’s oral collateral promise is within the suretyship Statute of Frauds because the facts show benefit to Lydia, not Paul.

C.signal: This looks at whether Paul personally received the money, not whether Barnabas gave bargained-for value.
C.lawyer: Consideration may be given to the borrower rather than to the guarantor.

D.signal: This grabs a different Statute of Frauds lane instead of the guaranty lane.
D.lawyer: The suretyship provision supplies the responsive defense; the one-year answer is not Paul’s best defense on these facts.

goldKeys.statement: An oral promise to answer for another person’s debt is usually inside the Statute of Frauds; the main-purpose exception removes it only when the guarantor’s leading purpose is the guarantor’s own economic advantage.
goldKeys.trigger: A speaker says, 'If the borrower does not pay, I will,' and no signed writing from that speaker appears.
goldKeys.unlocks: the primary-purpose defense and the suretyship writing gate

goldKeys.statement: Consideration does not have to move into the guarantor’s pocket; performance given to the borrower can support the guarantor’s promise if it was bargained for.
goldKeys.trigger: The guarantor points to receiving no money personally even though the lender gave the borrower the money after the guaranty.

silverKeys.statement: In a best-defense array, sort defenses by whose promise they attack: the guarantor’s promise beats borrower-loan defects when the lawsuit is against the guarantor.
silverKeys.trigger: The call asks for the guarantor’s best defense, but several choices attack the borrower’s loan.

remediation.title: Suretyship main-purpose gate
remediation.signal: If the borrower does not pay, I will.
remediation.studentMove: Ask whether the guarantor was mainly seeking personal economic advantage.
remediation.tinyRule: No self-benefit means oral guaranty stays in the writing-required bucket.
remediation.trap: no-consideration dominant trap and one-year bait
